text:
maya: CI red on nightly-smoke — seeing a bunch of H100 jobs fail with Xid=85 and sporadic 'invalid device function'. Some shards hit CUDA OOMs too. Anyone on triage?

ci-bot: Build: https://ci.redwood/example/12345 · failed tests: smoke/shard-7, smoke/shard-12 · last changed: refs/heads/main@f2c3b9 · logs: /artifacts/12345/logs.tar.gz

zach: I can take an initial look. Do we have the full container + driver combo used for the run? suspect driver/container skew.

maya: run used image gcr.io/redwood/nightly:2026-03-16 and driver 535.54.03 on canary. Attaching the small excerpt:
```
[2026-03-16 02:14:21] kernel: H100: GPU0 Xid=85: EC=0x1e
[2026-03-16 02:14:21] runtime: invalid device function
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
Aborted (core dumped)
```

kai: if it's intermittent across shards could be mem fragmentation. Before doing a full bisect, try rerunning the two impacted shards with a single job pinned to one GPU and CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 to get stack traces.

zach: agree — rerun shard-7 & shard-12 now? also add environment: NV_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 and set RLIMIT_MEMLOCK larger.

oliver: I can queue reruns. which commit range should we bisect if reruns reproduce? looks like we landed allocator tweaks in f2c3b9 -> e1a7d2 last week.

maya: queued reruns: https://ci.redwood/example/12345/retry-67890 · will report back in ~10m

ci-bot: Rerun queued by oliver · job: https://ci.redwood/example/12345/retry-67890 · status: running

sara: fwiw I rolled driver canary to 535.54.03 yesterday in infra-canary; we should test older driver (535.41.01) as a quick check. If older driver passes, likely kernel/driver interaction.

zach: good call — oliver can you spawn a quick job using the 535.41.01 host driver (we have an infra label h100-driver-535-41)? if that fails too, we'll bisect code.

oliver: started two matrix jobs: retry-67890-driver-old and retry-67890-driver-canary. linking: https://ci.redwood/example/12345/matrix · will grab dmesg if they fail.

ci-bot: Matrix jobs started · retry-67890-driver-old (node: h100-535-41-02) · retry-67890-driver-canary (node: h100-535-54-03-07)

maya: rerun logs (shard-7) attached: shows same Xid=85 + occasional small heap OOM before abort. Not deterministic — one run passed, then next failed after 30s.

kai: random pass/fail points to resource pressure / fragmentation + allocator change. If old-driver job passes consistently, it's likely driver/regression; otherwise try bisecting commits from f2c3b9 back to e1a7d2.

oliver: update: old-driver job passed 3/3, canary failed 2/3. dmesg from failing node shows repeated Xid=85 and nvlink warnings. uploading trace: /artifacts/12345/trace.tar.gz

zach: that's pretty telling. next steps: 1) schedule a controlled bisect of the allocator PRs 2) pin nightly to old driver for stability 3) create a short-term exp fallback to reduce batch sizes in smoke so end-to-end jobs pass.

maya: can someone pick the bisect? I can pin the driver for tonight and open a fallback PR to lower batch -> will prepare PR.

oliver: I’ll own the bisect. plan: binary-search commits between e1a7d2..f2c3b9 focusing on allocator and memory management files. I'll run quick smoke at each step on both drivers to confirm. If we get a single-commit repro, we can revert or fix.

sara: add a label bisect-needed and tag @eng-ml-allocator. also add a note in the incident board.

ci-bot: Created task: https://issues.redwood/INC-7891 · labels: bisect-needed, h100 · assignee: oliver

zach: thanks. oliver, if you need a fast local repro, try this launch:
```
docker run --gpus all -e CUDA_LAUNCH_BLOCKING=1 -e NV_BACKEND_MEMPOOL=1 gcr.io/redwood/nightly:2026-03-16 ./run_smoke --shard 7 --repeat 100
```
and collect `nvidia-smi dmon` + `dmesg -w` in another shell.

oliver: copying commands. I'll start bisect tomorrow morning and post progress here.

maya: thanks all — pinning driver and opening batch-size fallback PR now. Will post links. :thumbsup:

zach: nice coordination, will keep an eye on the bisect and help narrow if oliver finds a commit.

oliver: quick follow-up after initial bisect run (later): found a likely commit  e1f9a4 (allocator: use pooled remapping) that increases frag under long-lived KV caches. reproduces with canary driver, not with old driver. Filing PR to revert the change pending deeper fix.

maya: awesome find. can we get a hotfix revert and roll nightly back to stable driver? I'll coordinate with infra.

ci-bot: Hotfix PR created: https://ci.redwood/pr/4567 · revert e1f9a4 · checks queued.

maya: closing loop — rolled nightly to 535.41.01 and merged temporary revert. nightly-smoke green on next run. i'll follow-up with root-cause postmortem next week. thanks everyone.

zach: great job team.

oliver: noted root cause follow-up will include memory layout details and repro steps.

maya: thanks :heart:
